raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview Gemma 4 documents tool calls as `<|tool_call>call:name{key:value}`, but some checkpoints write the body in parentheses (`call:terminal(command:<|"|>ls -a<|"|>)`, vllm-project/vllm#53642). Python's parser accepts that form and the name-only `call:name` since vllm-project/vllm#53657. This PR brings the Rust Gemma 4 parser to the same behavior. ## Claims - The Rust Gemma 4 parser accepts parenthesized calls and name-only calls (empty arguments `{}`), in non-streaming and streaming at any chunk split. - A body must end with the closer that matches its opener; `call:f(x:1}` is rejected, as a braced body without `}` already was. ## Validation Commands from `.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh` (`style-clippy` and `test`), run from the repo root: ``` cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check # ok cargo sort --workspace --check rust # ok cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans # ok cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings # ok cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast # 2312 tests run: 2312 passed, 13 skipped ``` - `gemma4_accepts_parenthesized_and_name_only_calls_at_every_split`: a paren call whose string value contains parentheses, a name-only call and a braced call, parsed whole and at every two-chunk split; checks names, arguments and tool indexes. - `gemma4_parenthesized_call_requires_its_own_closer`: `call:set(flag:true}` fails, and `reset` returns the raw input. - Both tests fail on `main`. Python's PR added no unit test; its reproducer is covered by the first test. ## Details Root cause: the Rust header parser (`rust/src/parser/src/unified/gemma4.rs`) read the name up to `{` and required it. On the paren form the call never left the header state, so the request either failed at finish as an incomplete tool call, or a later braced call's `{` ended a garbage name (`terminal(command:...)<|tool_call>call:terminal`) carrying the second call's arguments. Change: the header ends at `{`, `(` or ``. The active call (`Gemma4CallBody`) remembers its opener, so the body must end with the matching closer, and `reset` reconstructs the raw text with that opener. The change stays in the model-specific parser; the generic argument grammar is unchanged. Deviation from Python: Python drops a trailing `}` regardless of the opener, and a trailing `)` whenever the raw arguments have more `)` than `(`, so it also accepts mixed brackets such as `call:f(x:1}`. Rust picks the closer from the opener and rejects a mismatch. No report shows a mixed form. Not a duplicate: no open PR changes the Rust Gemma 4 call header. AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to prepare this change; the human submitter reviewed every changed line. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_01K2SEJPm2Mawmm6pu8m9E1o ---
Pull Request Checklist - [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. - [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. - [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
